title: What happened
goal: Tell someone what you did and what happened, using the simple past and the ergative نے construction.
intro:
The Urdu past tense is simple to form but has one famous twist: the **ergative** construction. With *transitive* verbs (verbs that take an object, like 'eat', 'see', 'say'), the subject takes the marker **نے** and the verb agrees with the **object** instead of the subject: **میں نے چائے پی** 'I drank tea' — پی is feminine because چائے is feminine, whoever 'I' is.

It feels strange at first, but it is completely regular. Take it step by step: first intransitive verbs (go, come, sleep), then transitive verbs with نے.

vocab.en: to meet; to be found, get
vocab.note: کسی سے ملنا = to meet someone (no نے); مجھے مل گیا = I found it / got it
Takes نے; person addressed takes سے: اس نے مجھ سے کہا.
Person told takes کو: مجھے بتائیں.
Exception: never takes نے — میں لایا.
Usually without نے: میں بھول گیا.
f. مجھے یاد ہے = I remember; یاد آنا = to come to mind, miss
ختم ہونا = to end; ختم کرنا = to finish. Often pronounced 'xatam'.
f. پہلی بار = the first time; کئی بار = several times
Invariable. بند کرنا = to close, turn off

phrases.en: I've lost my phone. (lit. my phone got lost)

phrases.native: اس نے مجھے کچھ نہیں بتایا۔
phrases.roman: us ne mujhe kuchh nahīṃ batāyā.

phrases.native: میں پچھلے سال پاکستان آیا تھا۔
phrases.roman: maiṃ pichhle sāl Pākistān āyā thā.
phrases.en: I came to Pakistan last year. (man)

grammar.title: The simple past of intransitive verbs
grammar.body:
The simple past is **stem + ا -ā (m. sg) / ے -e (m. pl) / ی -ī (f. sg) / یں -īṃ (f. pl)**. With intransitive verbs (no object) it agrees with the subject, just like other tenses: وہ آیا 'he came', وہ آئی 'she came', وہ آئے 'they came'.

If the stem ends in a vowel, add **ی y** before -ā: آ → آیا āyā, سو → سویا soyā.

Irregular pasts to learn now: **جانا → گیا** gayā (گئی، گئے), **ہونا → ہوا** huā (ہوئی، ہوئے).

Very common: the past with the helper **جانا** for completed events: سو گیا 'fell asleep', ٹوٹ گیا 'broke', پہنچ گئے 'arrived', ختم ہو گیا 'was over'. Add **تھا** for 'had …' or a more distant past: وہ آیا تھا 'he had come / he came (back then)'.

examples.en: Mum went to the market. (respectful plural)

grammar.title: Transitive verbs: the ergative نے
grammar.body:
With **transitive** verbs in the past, the subject takes **نے** and the verb agrees with the **object**:

احمد **نے** روٹی کھائی 'Ahmed ate roti' — کھائی is feminine because روٹی is.
سارہ **نے** آم کھایا 'Sarah ate a mango' — کھایا is masculine because آم is.

Pronouns + نے: میں نے، ہم نے، تم نے، آپ نے، **اس نے** (he/she), **انہوں نے** (they / he-she respectful). (تو نے is rare.)

If the object itself has **کو** (a specific person or thing), or there's no object, the verb goes to the neutral **masculine singular**: میں نے اسے دیکھا 'I saw him/her'; اس نے کہا 'he/she said'.

Irregular pasts: **کرنا → کیا** kiyā (کی kī), **دینا → دیا** diyā, **لینا → لیا** liyā, **پینا → پیا** piyā.

Exceptions that **don't** take نے: لانا (bring), بولنا (speak — but with an object it does: اس نے جھوٹ بولا 'he lied'), بھولنا (forget), and compounds with جانا (کھا گیا).

examples.en: I drank tea. (پی agrees with f. چائے)

examples.native: انہوں نے مجھے ایک خط بھیجا۔
examples.roman: unhoṃ ne mujhe ek xat bhejā.

examples.en: The girl called the boys. (object with کو → neutral بلایا)

dialogue.title: How was the wedding?
dialogue.setting: Nida asks her colleague Faraz about his weekend.

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: بہت اچھا! ہم ملتان گئے، میرے کزن کی شادی تھی۔
lines.roman: bahut achchhā! ham Multān ga’e, mere kazan kī shādī thī.
lines.en: Very good! We went to Multan — it was my cousin's wedding.

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: میں نے شیروانی پہنی۔ امی نے خاص طور پر بنوائی تھی۔
lines.roman: maiṃ ne sherwānī pahnī. ammī ne xās taur par banvā’ī thī.
lines.en: I wore a sherwani. Mum had it specially made.

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: زبردست تھا۔ میں نے بہت زیادہ کھا لیا!
lines.roman: zabardast thā. maiṃ ne bahut zyāda khā liyā!
lines.en: Amazing. I ate far too much!

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: ہاں! اچانک بتی چلی گئی اور سب لوگ اندھیرے میں ناچتے رہے۔
lines.roman: hāṃ! achānak battī chalī ga’ī aur sab log andhere meṃ nāchte rahe.
lines.en: Yes! Suddenly the power went off and everyone kept dancing in the dark.

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: لیں، لیکن فون میں نہیں ہیں… میں فون گاڑی میں بھول گیا!
lines.roman: līṃ, lekin fon meṃ nahīṃ haiṃ… maiṃ fon gāṛī meṃ bhūl gayā!
lines.en: I did, but they're not on my phone… I left my phone in the car!

culture: Pakistani weddings typically last several days — مہندی (henna night with music and dancing), بارات (the groom's procession and the main ceremony, with نکاح the marriage contract) and ولیمہ (the reception hosted by the groom's family). Guests number in the hundreds, and wedding stories are a staple of conversation for weeks afterwards.
